reasons: Several steps only print a warning when they fail and then continue, so problems can be hidden.
The database setup uses a name, survey_tool, that differs from the name in the Docker setup.

terms.meaning: A private folder of Python packages for this project, so they do not clash with other projects.
A full database server that must be installed separately.
An add-on for PostgreSQL that stores numeric vectors for search.
A Linux command that runs another command with administrator rights.

used_by: Run by the owner from the project folder.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Environment checks and virtual environment
sections.what: Checks for Python 3 and PostgreSQL, tries to start PostgreSQL if it is stopped, then creates and activates a private Python environment for the project.
sections.why: Ensures the required tools are present before installing anything.
sections.watch_out: The version check only confirms that Python exists. It does not check that the version is 3.11 or newer, as the message claims.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Package install and settings file
sections.what: Updates pip, installs all packages from the requirements file, then creates the settings file if one does not exist. It asks the owner to edit the file in the nano text editor.
sections.why: The app needs its packages and settings before it can start.
sections.watch_out: The package install can take several minutes and prints nothing while it runs because output is hidden.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Database creation
sections.what: Asks for the PostgreSQL username and password, creates the survey_tool database, and turns on the vector and UUID add-ons.
sections.why: The app stores all its data in this database.
sections.watch_out: If the database already exists, the error is hidden and the script continues as if all went well.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Setup summary and reminders
sections.what: Prints a setup complete banner, the steps to start the server (activate venv, cd backend, run uvicorn), the docs URL, a documentation list, and reminders to configure .env and check the PostgreSQL password.
sections.why: Tells the user what to do after setup finishes.
sections.watch_out: This block only prints text; it does not create tables, load models or load sample data.

summary: A Mac or Linux script that installs the platform without Docker, using a local PostgreSQL database, a Python virtual environment and the settings file.
purpose: Lets the owner run the platform directly on their computer without Docker.
why: Likely reason: some owners prefer a native install, and the script automates the many steps.
how: The script checks Python and PostgreSQL, starts PostgreSQL if needed, creates a virtual environment, installs the Python packages, and creates the settings file. It then asks for database details, creates the database and extensions, creates the tables, loads the model list, and optionally loads sample data. Finally it prints the commands to start the server.
inputs: Database username and password typed at the prompts, and the settings file the owner edits.
outputs: A virtual environment, a local database named survey_tool, created tables, and a model list.
risks: The password is passed through an environment variable to the database tool, so it may be visible to other programs on the same machine. The script runs sudo on Linux to start PostgreSQL.
debug: If the database step fails, confirm the username and password and that PostgreSQL is running. If tables are not created, check the DATABASE_URL value in the settings file. If packages fail, rerun the install step and read its error.
